what_happened: The operator wrote two requests by hand and queued them: an auditor fix (20261017-182608-jjkf) and an independent review of docs/design/job-planning.md (20261017-182610-6cd8). Each had the requirements, the plan and behavioral acceptance that a planning stage would have produced. The operator did this because Athena does not yet plan its own work (OP-17). An independent spot-check found the auditor defect, and the operator confirmed it. No job failed. The operator supplied the design work as an intervention.
cause: Athena has no stage between a short outcome request and the producer that turns the outcome into requirements, a plan and behavioral acceptance. Until one exists, the only place that work can happen is the operator. Defects are also found only by outside spot-checks, because Athena does not audit its own auditor. The operator fills the planning gap because it is the only way to get well-formed jobs. That makes the operator Athena's planner, and the judgment never moves into Athena.
prevention: Add a planning stage that runs before the producer. It takes a one- or two-line outcome request and writes the requirements, the plan and behavioral acceptance criteria. An independent critique step reviews the plan, and the operator approves it only when needed. Until that stage exists, log each hand-planned request as an intervention at the moment it is queued, so the count reflects the real planning burden.
proposed_request: Build a planning stage for Athena jobs. When a request is admitted, Athena should produce a written plan before any code is written. The plan should state the requirements, the steps, and acceptance criteria that check behavior, not just that parts exist. A separate critique pass should review the plan against the request and the repo docs, including docs/design/job-planning.md, and record its findings. The producer should start only from a plan that passed critique. Show it working on the auditor fix (20261017-182608-jjkf) from a two-line outcome request, with no operator-written plan, and confirm the plan it produces covers the defect found in the spot-check.
